predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: the Crown's Ulster, granted to Walter de Burgh in 1263; the page also records an earlier title granted to John de Courcy in 1181

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: 'By the 15th century the earldom was restricted to coastal enclaves' in Down and around Carrickfergus; the title of Earl of Ulster 'passed to the Crown in 1461'

ledger.x: 1263: Walter de Burgh is granted the earldom of Ulster.
1333: the earldom collapses with the murder of William Donn de Burgh.

wars.name: Bruce invasion of Ulster
wars.outcome: Peace 'ended with a siege of Carrickfergus Castle by Edward Bruce in 1315'; the campaign of the 1310s caused 'heavy damage from which the earldom never recovered'.

wars.name: Burke Civil War
wars.outcome: After William Donn was killed in June 1333 his de Burgh kinsmen 'began the Burke Civil War for supremacy' (William had had his cousin Sir Walter Liath de Burgh starved to death at Greencastle, near the mouth of Lough Foyle, in February 1332).

certainty.note: A feudal earldom whose extent is described only as 'most of' Antrim and Down, briefly west to Lough Foyle; no survey or treaty line.

sources.title: William Donn de Burgh, 3rd Earl of Ulster
